title: Pokopia Patch Notes & Version History Guide
description: Read the full Pokopia Ver. 2.0.0 patch notes from August 5, 2026, plus bug fixes and update history. See the latest changes and older versions.
content: Guides Home Guides Pokopia Patch Notes & Version History About Pokopia 2026-08-09 Pokopia Patch Notes & Version History Read the full Pokopia Ver. 2.0.0 patch notes from August 5, 2026, plus bug fixes and update history. See the latest changes and older versions. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Get patch notes on Discord Receive full patch notes and update alerts as soon as a new version is posted. Join our Discord Update History This page tracks the latest Pokopia update details. New versions will be added here as soon as they are available. Ver. 2.0.0 (August 5, 2026) Additions Added all content for the Expansion Pass - Bubbly Basin Added the move Dive, allowing players to move freely underwater. The Build specialty can now be used to build houses underwater. Added new items such as the portal pod and safe. Added the new pattern, dynamic Ditto print. Added new emotes: Lie Down and Ready, Set, Go! Added five new hair colors: orange, light pink, yellow-green, blue-green, and brown. Added a function to move items in bulk between the storage box and bag. Added a function to delete items placed inside objects such as the garbage bin. Added the ability to fine-tune depth placement when placing windows, doors, and similar items. Added an option in Settings to hide the confirmation message shown when canceling Magnet Rise. Added an option in Settings allowing movement while the move wheel is open. Added motion-sickness reduction settings for the camera. The following items can now be painted: stylish stool, handrail, metal chain, workbench, vending machine, bike, bookcase, Pokémon Center counter, arrow sign, rope. Improvements Even if a Pokémon's habitat is destroyed, it will move back in if the same habitat is rebuilt within a certain area. Pokémon that are sad because furniture was removed will now notice more quickly when the same furniture is replaced. Pokémon that taught you an emote will now respond with the same emote when you use it. If a Pokémon being searched for in the Pokédex is in another town, you can now travel to that town using Return Home. Reduced ordinary conversation indicators so that special Pokémon conversations and requests directed at Ditto stand out more clearly. Lost relics can now be appraised in batches of up to 10 at a time. Paint, Gather Honey, and Collect can now be performed multiple times in the same interaction. During crafting, materials in the storage box next to the workbench will be consumed before materials in the bag. Increased the placement limit for power generators (excluding furnaces) from 64 to 128. Increased the number of different photos that can be displayed in a town from 10 to 40. When sucking up liquid, a short press of the move button to hold liquids in Ditto's mouth will allow liquid to be held in their mouth without removing it from the environment. When releasing stored water, adjusted water levels now automatically match nearby water levels. Smearguru can now learn patterns from photos stored in References. Improved visibility of the target item when painting with paint balloons. Increased the amount of treasure discoverable with the Dowsing Machine on Dream Islands. Pokémon companions can now follow you while moving with Surf, Glide, Rollout, or Magnet Rise. Inhaling items and opening the bag are now possible while rolling using Rollout. Rollout can now destroy certain natural objects such as large boulders. Surf can now be activated on land by pressing the Surf button while holding the focus button. Improved activation conditions for Surf and Waterfall so they occur more smoothly. Leafage can now be used on farm soil to revert it to a normal soil block. Strength can now be used underwater. Added an All tab to both the Pokédex and Habitat Dex. Made it clearer that buildings can still be remodeled even when items such as the Ditto Flag are attached to roofs or walls. During construction, any Pokémon not assigned to the Build role in a building project can now help with cooking. Prevented treasures in Sparkling Skylands from appearing when using the Dowsing Machine in locations where breaking terrain would cause them to fall. Improved messaging when there are insufficient materials for copying items using the 3D Printer. Items can now be placed on top of square plants. Hide-and-sneak can now be canceled midway. Adjusted in-game event notifications shown at startup so they are displayed only during specific remaining-day periods. Certain roof items now block water. Increased output when crafting curved eaves to 10. Tidal Bell and Clear Bell can now be triggered using laser sensors and switches. Adjusted sound effects for camping chair and sleeping bag. Improved performance for certain rendering processes. Fixes When talking to a Pokémon that is currently assigned to construct buildings, options such as "Follow me!" may sometimes fail to appear. Suicune and Gholdengo may be unable to travel across water. Pokémon may occasionally fall into the ocean or off cliffs when appearing from their habitats. Even when using honey, Pokémon may sometimes fail to return to their habitats. Using Magnet Rise may occasionally cause Pokémon to scold or warn the player. Pokémon that dislike water may sometimes be unable to move across duckweed and flowering duckweed on the water's surface. Requests from Pokémon may occasionally ask for items that the requesting Pokémon actually dislikes. When processing berries in the community box, paint may not be produced correctly. The timing of the note played by the music mat (high Do) is offset incorrectly. Certain furniture can be painted through specific procedures even on parts where the colors are not actually changeable. Painting certain items may use more paint than intended. The light color of a painted surface light may fail to change correctly. Under specific conditions, it is possible to place more than one party cooking pot in the same town. Some items may display unnaturally when viewed from a distance. For some items, visual effects may disappear when viewed through glass. Under certain conditions during multiplayer, building may become impossible to complete or cancel. In certain situations, it may be unclear why actions such as building or relocation cannot be performed. On Cloud Islands, players other than the administrator may be able to place a relocation kit. Under certain conditions, a building kit may become unrecoverable when remodeling a house. Under certain conditions, painted portions of the sand house may be reset. Using Rock Smash while falling may cause Ditto's position or height to become significantly displaced. During the Withered Wasteland request "Clear the path!" Slowpoke may stop moving partway through. During the Sparkling Skylands request "Follow Tinkmaster!" certain actions may prevent the request from progressing. During the Sparkling Skylands request "Pokémon Center tour guide!" searching for Tinkmaster in the Pokédex may guide the player to the town containing their habitat rather than the town where they are currently located. Loading may occasionally fail to finish when returning from a Dream Island. Returning from a Dream Island may incorrectly send the player to Palette Town. Under certain conditions when an online session ends, the player may be transported to a Dream Island. On the Cloud Island loading screen, the player's gender pronoun may sometimes be displayed incorrectly in some languages. Notes This update is required for your game to go online. Ver. 1.1.1 (June 19, 2026) Fixes The following issues have been fixed Fixed an issue areas may not act correctly if too many items over a limit are placed Fixed an issue where Ditto may not change expressions in photo mode when using an emote. Notes This update is required for your game to go online. Ver. 1.1.0 (June 9, 2026) Adds ability to purchase Pokémon Pokopia's Expansion Pass Adds the Dynamic Ditto Print & Dynamic Ditto Print (Wallpaper) items Added new conversation variations between Pokémon. Added and adjusted conversation variations for Pokémon with a "..." speech bubble. Pokémon accompanying Ditto can now use chairs and beds together where possible. Vaporeon, Jolteon, Flareon, Espeon, Umbreon, Glaceon, and Sylveon will now sleep at the edge of sofas, similar to Leafeon. Pokémon accompanying Ditto will now avoid the placement preview area when objects are being placed. When moving Pokémon into a two-storey house, players can now choose the destination floor while indoors. Pokémon processing materials at the community box or furnace will now prioritise locations closer to their own habitat. If Ditto's transformation wears off while falling, pressing the Run or Jump button will return Ditto to human form and restore control. Increased the placement limit for items that use electricity from 512 to 1,024. The laser sensor item now displays its detection range when being placed. Fixes The following issues have been fixed Fixed an issue where Pokémon could stop partway through processing materials from the community box. Fixed an issue where transactions at the Pokémon Center or Poké Mart could end immediately. Fixed an issue where Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff could be unable to move through the air. content: Guides Home Guides How to Get Copper Ore in Pokémon Pokopia: Complete Guide Resources & How to Get 2026-06-06 How to Get Copper Ore in Pokémon Pokopia: Complete Guide Learn where to find Copper Ore in Pokémon Pokopia and how to farm it fast. Mine copper with Rock Smash in Rocky Ridges and Rocky Dream Island, then smelt it into Copper Bars. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Copper Ore is a key mining material in Pokémon Pokopia, used to craft the Pokémon Center rebuild kit, the Fountain Plaza kit, and Scrap blocks. It's smelted into Copper Bars for higher-tier recipes. This guide covers where to find Copper Ore, how to mine it efficiently, and how to process it. Where to Find Copper Ore Copper Ore is mined from copper-bearing rocks — gray boulders with orange-brown copper veins running through them. There are two main locations: Location How to Access Notes Rocky Ridges Town Story progression (3rd area) Found in the mine and around the rocky terrain Rocky Dream Island Use the Clefairy Doll with Drifloon Best farming spot — resets daily How to Mine Copper Ore To break copper-bearing rocks, you need the Rock Smash move (learned from Hitmonchan during the Rocky Ridges story). Good news: Unlike harder ores such as Gold or Iron, Copper Ore rocks can be broken with a non-powered Rock Smash . You don't need to eat a Hamburger Steak first — though powering up still speeds things up. Each copper rock you break drops Copper Ore that you pick up with Y . Best Way to Farm Copper Ore (Recommended) The most efficient method is mining at Rocky Dream Island : Find or obtain the Clefairy Doll (Piepi Doll) and show it to Drifloon to travel to Rocky Dream Island Eat a Hamburger Steak to power up Rock Smash and Rollout for faster mining Use Rollout to plow through copper deposits on the ground and inside the island quickly Break wall-mounted copper rocks with Rock Smash Return the next day — Dream Islands reset at 5:00 AM , so the copper respawns See the full Dream Island guide for all doll locations and island types. Tip: If you don't want to wait for the daily reset, change the date on your Nintendo Switch 2 to refresh the island and mine again immediately. How to Smelt Copper Ore into Copper Bars Most advanced recipes require Copper Bars , not raw Copper Ore. To smelt: Place the Copper Ore into a Blast Furnace Assign a Pokémon with the Burn specialty (such as Growlithe, Torchic, or Magmar) Wait for processing — 1 Copper Ore = 1 Copper Bar What Copper Ore Is Used For Use Materials Required Scrap block Crafting material Fountain Plaza Kit Lumber ×20, Stone ×20, Copper ×20 Pokémon Center Rebuild Kit Stone ×25, Iron ×25, Copper ×25, Crystal ×5 Copper Bar recipes Smelt first, then use in furniture and tools Quick Tips Farm at Rocky Dream Island — it's the most efficient and resets every day Eat a Hamburger Steak — powering up Rollout lets you collect copper in bulk Stockpile early — the Pokémon Center rebuild kit alone needs 25 Copper Smelt in batches — assign a Burn Pokémon to the Blast Furnace and process multiple ores at once Use the date-change trick — refresh the Dream Island instantly instead of waiting for the 5 AM reset Previous Resources & How to Get How to Make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia: Mixer & Limestone Next Gameplay Guides How to Get the Game Boy in Pokopia & All Uses Found incorrect data? title: How to Get Ice in Pokémon Pokopia Guide
description: How to get Ice in Pokémon Pokopia. Two confirmed locations — Palette Town's secret cave and Rock Peak Dream Island — plus Freezing Chambers build requirements for Articuno.
content: Guides Home Guides How to Get Ice in Pokémon Pokopia Resources & How to Get 2026-05-10 How to Get Ice in Pokémon Pokopia How to get Ice in Pokémon Pokopia. Two confirmed locations — Palette Town's secret cave and Rock Peak Dream Island — plus Freezing Chambers build requirements for Articuno. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Ice is one of the harder materials to find in Pokopia because it only appears in two specific locations. It is also one of the most important — you need 50 Ice to build the Freezing Chambers , the construction required to unlock Articuno . Do not spend Ice on decoration until you have secured enough for the build. Fast Answer Primary source: Secret cave behind the waterfall in Palette Town — hundreds of Ice blocks available Secondary source: Rock Peak Dream Island via Drifloon (requires Clefairy Doll) — smaller amount inside the rocky structure at the center Location 1: Palette Town Secret Cave (Best Source) This is by far the most efficient Ice farming spot in the game. How to reach it: Head to Palette Town (accessible via the road through Withered Wastelands) Find the waterfall on the eastern side of the area Move to the right side of the waterfall and look for a Glow Mushroom Walk toward it — you will enter a hidden passage Follow the path inside to reach a large chamber filled with Ice blocks and Crystal Shards This room respawns its resources, making it the go-to farming spot whenever you need to restock Ice. Location 2: Rock Peak Dream Island (Secondary Source) A smaller but reliable supplement if you are already farming Dream Islands. Requirements: Access to Drifloon's Dream Island system Clefairy Doll (required to unlock Rock Peak Dream Island) Once on Rock Peak Dream Island, find the rocky structure at the center of the island. Ice blocks are located inside. The yield is smaller than the Palette Town cave, but it is worth picking up if you are running the island for other resources. What Ice Is Used For Freezing Chambers (Articuno Habitat) The primary use for Ice is building the Freezing Chambers — the large construction kit that causes Articuno to appear. This is a required step for full Pokédex completion. Materials needed: Material Amount Stone ×50 Ice ×50 Crystal Shard ×10 Pokemetal ×10 Pokémon crew required: 1× Pokémon with Build specialty 1× Pokémon with Water specialty 1× Pokémon with Search specialty 12× any additional Pokémon Total: 15 Pokémon Construction takes approximately one in-game day. Because of its large size, clear and flatten a wide open area before placing the kit. Where to find the kit: The Freezing Chambers kit is located on the eastern island where you first arrive in Palette Town. After Building Once the Freezing Chambers is complete, Articuno appears inside. It prefers a Cool environment, so place cool-type furniture nearby to raise its comfort level. Farming Tips Do the Palette Town cave first — it gives you 50 Ice in a single run, which is exactly what you need for the Freezing Chambers Pick up Crystal Shards at the same time — the secret cave contains both Ice and Crystal Shards, letting you farm two Freezing Chambers materials in one trip Save Ice before decorating — Ice can be used for decoration, but secure your 50 for the build first Rock Peak Dream Island is a bonus stop , not a primary route — use it when you are already there for other items like Seashells or Twine Related Guides Palette Town Guide Dream Island Guide How to Get Crystal Fragments All Crafting Materials in Pokémon Pokopia Previous Gameplay Guides Pokopia CoroCoro Island Guide: Address Code & All Items Next Gameplay Guides Pokopia Public Island Codes: All Official Virtual Mode Addresses Found incorrect data? description: Learn how to make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia. Craft the Concrete Mixer, farm Limestone efficiently, use a Crush Pokémon, and see how much Concrete every kit needs.
content: Guides Home Guides How to Make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia: Mixer & Limestone Resources & How to Get 2026-06-11 How to Make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia: Mixer & Limestone Learn how to make Concrete in Pokémon Pokopia. Craft the Concrete Mixer, farm Limestone efficiently, use a Crush Pokémon, and see how much Concrete every kit needs. Author : Pokopia Guide Team Concrete is one of the most-needed building materials in Pokémon Pokopia. You'll burn through it building houses, lift stations, elevators, and the larger town kits. This guide covers how to make Concrete, where to farm Limestone fast, and exactly how much Concrete each recipe needs. How to Make Concrete Concrete is produced by putting Limestone into a Concrete Mixer . Three things are required: A crafted Concrete Mixer The mixer placed next to water A Pokémon with the Crush specialty (such as Conkeldurr ) in that town Add Limestone to the mixer, bring over your Crush Pokémon, and it will grind the Limestone into Concrete. The mixer only works when placed next to water . If nothing happens, check that it's at the water's edge and that a Crush Pokémon lives in that town. How to Get the Concrete Mixer The Concrete Mixer recipe is learned during the Sparkling Skylands story, when you accept Conkeldurr's request . Once unlocked, craft it at a workbench and you can make as many mixers as you need. Tip: Crafting multiple Concrete Mixers lets you process several batches of Limestone at once — the single biggest time-saver for bulk Concrete. Where to Find Limestone Limestone is the bottleneck for Concrete, so knowing the best sources matters: Location Notes Rocky Dream Island Most efficient — use the Clefairy Doll, resets daily Rocky Ridges Town Inside the hot spring cave Sparkling Skylands Southeast of Tinkmaster's house Limestone comes from breaking the white striped rocks with Rock Smash. Best Way to Farm Limestone (and Concrete) The fastest method is farming Rocky Dream Island : Use the Clefairy Doll with Drifloon to travel to Rocky Dream Island Break all the Limestone rocks and collect everything Return home and feed it into your Concrete Mixers Come back the next day — the island resets at 5:00 AM , so Limestone respawns If you don't want to wait, change the date on your Nintendo Switch 2 to refresh the island and farm again immediately. How Much Concrete You Need Concrete is required in large amounts as you progress. Some key recipes: Recipe Concrete Needed House Foundation 1 White Line Path (vertical / horizontal) 2 each Lift Station 5 Elevator Station 8 Yellow Hut Kit 10 City House Kit 20 Grand City Kit 25 Because the bigger kits each need 10–25 Concrete, it pays to stockpile Limestone early. Quick Tips Build multiple Concrete Mixers — process Limestone in parallel Farm Rocky Dream Island daily — the most reliable Limestone source Keep a Crush Pokémon in town — Conkeldurr is the standard choice Place mixers at the water's edge — they won't run otherwise Stockpile before big builds — the Grand City Kit alone needs 25 Concrete For the related Control Unit and Paper materials, see the Paper, Concrete & Control Unit guide .
